# Operate the saved work queue

This short instruction file is trial-specific integration around the unmodified
Compound Engineering plugin. It is not a shipped CE queue feature.

1. Read docs/plans/*.md from disk. Their status, dependencies, workflow and
   named context sources are authoritative. Never infer approval from time.
2. A ready or in-progress plan is eligible only when all named dependencies
   are complete. Leave awaiting-human plans alone and continue other work.
3. Execute one eligible plan at a time in a fresh Agent context using the
   loaded compound-engineering:ce-work skill with
   `mode:return-to-caller <absolute-plan-path>`. Pass the exact skill path if
   the worker cannot resolve its name. The worker must read the skill and
   its required phase references, not replace them with an improvised process.
4. The worker follows the plan's named sources, verifies the actual output,
   and writes its working state/evidence before returning. Code and non-code
   plans keep their different execution paths. Local commits on trial/work
   are authorized. Shared knowledge cannot change as part of ordinary work.
5. Inspect the returned evidence and actual files. Mark a verified plan
   complete and preserve its output/evidence paths in the plan. Record a
   missing input or failure as a blocker on that plan. Do not silently clear
   it or block unrelated eligible plans. Commit only the trial's own files.
6. Re-read the queue after each completed plan so a newly satisfied dependency
   can run. Stop when nothing is eligible. Save reports/queue.md with completed,
   waiting and blocked plans. A fresh invocation starts from these files and
   skips completed work; do not rely on any previous coordinator conversation.

Preflight complete. No changes were made.

## Capability preflight: `compound-engineering:ce-work`

**Local README** (`README.md`): "Cedar Workshop — synthetic trial fixture." Python stdlib only, invented data, tests via `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. Nothing in it constrains the skill.

**Plugin skill path**
`/tmp/coga-adoption-ce-20260911/skills/ce-work/SKILL.md` — reported by the harness as the skill's base directory when loaded. It is *outside* the candidate repo (`/tmp/coga-adoption-trial-20260911/candidate`), which is why file search inside the repo didn't find it. All 13 bundled references are present under `references/`.

**Knowledge-work support: yes, via an explicit carve-out**
`references/input-triage.md:44-46` routes any plan whose metadata carries `execution: knowledge-work` to `references/non-code-execution.md` (present on disk) instead of the code lifecycle. Two caveats:
- It's triggered by plan **metadata**, not by prompt content. A bare prompt with no plan goes through `work-intake.md` as code work.
- Blank invocation will *not* auto-select a knowledge-work plan; it stops and asks for an explicit path (`input-triage.md:49`).

**Return-to-Caller mode avoids remote publishing: yes**
Activated by a leading `mode:return-to-caller <plan-path>` token (`input-triage.md:27`). Per `SKILL.md` and `references/return-to-caller.md`:
- Performs implementation and local verification only; explicitly must not run simplify, code review, commit, PR creation, CI watching, or babysitting — "the caller owns those steps" (`return-to-caller.md:3-5`).
- Returns a structured result ending with `standalone_shipping_skipped: true` (`return-to-caller.md:28`).
- Won't print a copy-paste prompt for external engines; any engine used "must not open a PR" (`return-to-caller.md:32`).
- On a pre-existing dirty file collision it returns `blocked` rather than editing or committing it (`SKILL.md` Phase 1).

One thing to note for the trial: the skill *can* make local commits in return-to-caller mode (unit-scoped, per `implementation-loop.md` rules) — it avoids **push/PR**, not all git writes. If the trial needs a no-commit guarantee, that's a separate constraint to state at invocation time.

Stopping here as requested.

Its universal rule ("lowercase every pass ID… for all provider imports") is what put `.lower()` into `count_confirmed` and under-counted CedarPass v2 (`{"confirmed": 2}` vs. the correct 3). The code docstring now explains CedarPass, but an agent following CLAUDE.md's "consult accepted lessons under docs/solutions" would still read the old doc and reintroduce the bug — so the counterfactual holds. Updated in place rather than duplicated.

**Changed files** (uncommitted, in this worktree only):
- `docs/solutions/pass-identity.md` — rewritten from `evidence/operator-note.md`, `reports/01.md`, `attendance.py`, `tests/test_attendance.py`, and commit `be30bd8`. Kept the original `title`/`date`/`tags`, added `last_updated` plus the schema fields (`module`, `problem_type: convention`, `component`, `severity`, `applies_when`).

Nothing else touched: no code, no other plans, no settings, no commit, no remote.

**Exact proposed durable rule** (as written in the doc's Guidance section):

> Pass-ID identity is a per-provider rule. Apply only the rule confirmed for the feed you are counting; do not carry one provider's case handling to another.
> - **CedarPass v2** (current feed, `data/checkins.csv`, `attendance.py`): IDs are opaque and case-sensitive. `A7` and `a7` are two passes. Compare IDs exactly. Strip surrounding whitespace (transport noise). Exact duplicate confirmed rows are one pass. Count only rows whose `status` is `confirmed`; waitlist and canceled rows are not attendees. Source: `evidence/operator-note.md`, confirmed with the operator.
> - **LegacyPass** (older feed, `data/legacy.csv`): its import convention treated IDs case-insensitively. That convention is unchanged. No code in this repo currently consumes `data/legacy.csv`, so it is not implemented in `attendance.py`.
> - **Any other provider:** there is no default. Get the provider's identity rule confirmed and record it here before deduplicating.

Observed vs. unsupported: the CedarPass v2 case-sensitivity rule is stated as observed (operator note + red/green tests + fixture). The LegacyPass rule is stated as an unchanged convention with the explicit caveat that no code exercises it. The old "all providers" claim is called out as never verified, and the doc deliberately does not replace it with the opposite universal ("all providers are case-sensitive").

One note for the human reviewer: adding the schema frontmatter fields goes slightly beyond "preserve frontmatter structure"; they're additive and the parser-safety check passes, but drop them if you want the doc to stay in the original minimal shape.

 # Attendee identity
 
-Normalize every pass ID to lowercase before deduplication. This is the shared
-identity rule for all provider imports. Strip transport whitespace. Ignore
-waitlist and canceled rows when counting confirmed passes.
+## Context
 
-This convention came from the LegacyPass feed's case-insensitive identifiers.
+This lesson was written on 2026-09-01 when LegacyPass was the only provider.
+It said to lowercase every pass ID before deduplication and called that the
+shared rule for all provider imports. That universal claim was never verified
+for other providers, and it was wrong for CedarPass v2: `attendance.py`
+lowercased IDs, folded `A7` and `a7` into one pass, and reported
+`{"confirmed": 2}` for `data/checkins.csv` when the correct count is 3
+(`reports/01.md`, plan `docs/plans/01-count.md`, fix commit `be30bd8`).
+
+## Guidance
+
+Pass-ID identity is a per-provider rule. Apply only the rule confirmed for the
+feed you are counting; do not carry one provider's case handling to another.
+
+- **CedarPass v2** (current feed, `data/checkins.csv`, `attendance.py`):
+  IDs are opaque and case-sensitive. `A7` and `a7` are two passes. Compare IDs
+  exactly. Strip surrounding whitespace (transport noise). Exact duplicate
+  confirmed rows are one pass. Count only rows whose `status` is `confirmed`;
+  waitlist and canceled rows are not attendees. Source:
+  `evidence/operator-note.md`, confirmed with the operator.
+- **LegacyPass** (older feed, `data/legacy.csv`): its import convention treated
+  IDs case-insensitively (`Z9` and `z9` are one pass). That convention is
+  unchanged. No code in this repo currently consumes `data/legacy.csv`, so it
+  is not implemented in `attendance.py`.
+- **Any other provider:** there is no default. Get the provider's identity rule
+  confirmed and record it here before deduplicating.
+
+Whitespace stripping and excluding non-confirmed rows are the parts of the
+original lesson that held for both providers.
+
+## Why This Matters
+
+Lowercasing looks like harmless normalization, but for a case-sensitive
+provider it merges distinct attendees and under-counts. The old wording
+("shared identity rule for all provider imports") is exactly what led the
+count code to lowercase CedarPass IDs. A future agent following this doc as a
+universal rule would reintroduce the bug.
+
+## When to Apply
+
+- Before touching `count_confirmed` or any other dedup of pass IDs
+- When importing a new feed: treat case handling as an unknown until confirmed
+- When a LegacyPass importer is added: keep it case-insensitive; do not reuse
+  the CedarPass path unchanged
+
+## Examples
+
+```python
+# CedarPass v2 (attendance.py): exact comparison after strip
+len({row["pass_id"].strip() for row in rows if row["status"] == "confirmed"})
+
+# Previous, wrong for CedarPass v2: .lower() folded A7 and a7 together
+len({row["pass_id"].strip().lower() for row in rows if row["status"] == "confirmed"})
+```
+
+`tests/test_attendance.py` pins the CedarPass v2 behavior:
+`test_differently_cased_ids_are_separate_passes`,
+`test_surrounding_whitespace_is_transport_noise`,
+`test_non_confirmed_rows_are_excluded`, `test_checkins_fixture_counts_three`.
+
+## Related
+
+- `evidence/operator-note.md` — provider decision (authoritative for CedarPass v2)
+- `reports/01.md` — red/green evidence for the fix
+- `docs/plans/01-count.md` — the task that surfaced the stale rule

# Attendee identity

## Context

This lesson was written on 2026-09-01 when LegacyPass was the only provider.
It said to lowercase every pass ID before deduplication and called that the
shared rule for all provider imports. That universal claim was never verified
for other providers, and it was wrong for CedarPass v2: `attendance.py`
lowercased IDs, folded `A7` and `a7` into one pass, and reported
`{"confirmed": 2}` for `data/checkins.csv` when the correct count is 3
(`reports/01.md`, plan `docs/plans/01-count.md`, fix commit `be30bd8`).

## Guidance

Pass-ID identity is a per-provider rule. Apply only the rule confirmed for the
feed you are counting; do not carry one provider's case handling to another.

- **CedarPass v2** (current feed, `data/checkins.csv`, `attendance.py`):
  IDs are opaque and case-sensitive. `A7` and `a7` are two passes. Compare IDs
  exactly. Strip surrounding whitespace (transport noise). Exact duplicate
  confirmed rows are one pass. Count only rows whose `status` is `confirmed`;
  waitlist and canceled rows are not attendees. Source:
  `evidence/operator-note.md`, confirmed with the operator.
- **LegacyPass** (older feed, `data/legacy.csv`): its import convention treated
  IDs case-insensitively (`Z9` and `z9` are one pass). That convention is
  unchanged. No code in this repo currently consumes `data/legacy.csv`, so it
  is not implemented in `attendance.py`.
- **Any other provider:** there is no default. Get the provider's identity rule
  confirmed and record it here before deduplicating.

Whitespace stripping and excluding non-confirmed rows are the parts of the
original lesson that held for both providers.

## Why This Matters

Lowercasing looks like harmless normalization, but for a case-sensitive
provider it merges distinct attendees and under-counts. The old wording ("shared identity rule for all provider imports") would
instruct a future agent to lowercase CedarPass IDs and could reintroduce
the bug. The available evidence does not establish whether the document
caused the original implementation mistake.

## When to Apply

- Before touching `count_confirmed` or any other dedup of pass IDs
- When importing a new feed: treat case handling as an unknown until confirmed
- When a LegacyPass importer is added: keep it case-insensitive; do not reuse
  the CedarPass path unchanged

## Examples

```python
# CedarPass v2 (attendance.py): exact comparison after strip
len({row["pass_id"].strip() for row in rows if row["status"] == "confirmed"})

# Previous, wrong for CedarPass v2: .lower() folded A7 and a7 together
len({row["pass_id"].strip().lower() for row in rows if row["status"] == "confirmed"})
```

`tests/test_attendance.py` pins the CedarPass v2 behavior:
`test_differently_cased_ids_are_separate_passes`,
`test_surrounding_whitespace_is_transport_noise`,
`test_non_confirmed_rows_are_excluded`, `test_checkins_fixture_counts_three`.

## Related

- `evidence/operator-note.md` — provider decision (authoritative for CedarPass v2)
- `reports/01.md` — red/green evidence for the fix
- `docs/plans/01-count.md` — the task that surfaced the stale rule
